1 | # Waypoint — Adaptive Codebase Onboarding
     2 | 
     3 | Waypoint turns Python, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS repositories into an
     4 | evidence-aware code graph and a role-specific onboarding workspace. It uses
     5 | static analysis only: analyzed repository code is never imported or executed.
     6 | 
     7 | ## Architecture
     8 | 
     9 | ```mermaid
    10 | flowchart TD
    11 |     UI[React + TypeScript UI] -->|HTTP /api/v1| API[FastAPI application]
    12 |     API --> IMPORT[Local path or secured GitHub clone]
    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]
    26 |     VALIDATE --> UI
    27 |     UI --> COMPARE[Independent two-agent comparison]
    28 |     COMPARE --> TOOLS
    29 |     MCP[MCP server: 30 tools] --> GRAPH
    30 |     MCP --> SEARCH
    31 |     HOOKS[Pre / post / error hooks and JSONL traces] -.observe.-> API
    32 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> AGENT
    33 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> TOOLS
    34 | ```
    35 | 
    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,
    39 | chunks, lexical/vector indexes, issues, and conversation memory. The model layer supports
    40 | OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, and the Claude Agent SDK. In dual mode a low-cost model can
    41 | investigate through tools while a stronger model synthesizes a validated answer.
    42 | 
    43 | The detailed verification package, including coverage, Flask HTTP E2E, live multi-step
    44 | agent evidence, and same-question two-model comparison, is in
    45 | [`verification/README.md`](verification/README.md). Significant AI-assisted engineering
    46 | interactions are recorded in [`prompts.md`](prompts.md).
    47 | 
    48 | ## What is included
    49 | 
    50 | - Python AST extraction for modules, classes, functions, methods, imports, and calls
    51 | - Tree-sitter extraction for JavaScript/JSX, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS
    52 | - ES module imports/re-exports, CommonJS `require`, Java packages/imports, lexical
    53 |   containment, and conservatively inferred calls
    54 | - Explicit class-instantiation edges plus locally constructed receiver resolution for
    55 |   cross-file Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Java method calls
    56 | - Exact source spans, confidence, and unresolved-reference diagnostics
    57 | - Scalable React Flow visualization with on-demand neighborhood expansion
    58 | - Read-only Monaco source viewer and evidence inspector
    59 | - Claude-powered repository Q&A with bounded retrieval tools and validated citations
    60 | - revision-aware SQLite code indexing with persisted chunks, symbols, edges, file
    61 |   hashes, FTS5/BM25 search, and automatic refresh when repository contents change
    62 | - local subword-vector retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion, graph expansion, index
    63 |   status/rebuild controls, and restart-safe issue/onboarding state
    64 | - pre/post/error function hooks, correlated model/tool/retrieval traces, rotating JSONL
    65 |   diagnostics, and a 30-tool MCP connector over stdio or Streamable HTTP
    66 | - readable GitHub-flavored Markdown rendering …<1000 chars truncated>

1 | # External repository benchmarks
     2 | 
     3 | This suite validates the analyzer against shallow clones of established Python
     4 | repositories. Clones live outside the application workspace by default at
     5 | `C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks`.
     6 | 
     7 | The benchmark verifies:
     8 | 
     9 | - Parse success and performance
    10 | - Unique, stable node and edge identities
    11 | - Valid graph endpoints
    12 | - Valid source spans
    13 | - Evidence-status invariants
    14 | - Correct package names for flat and `src/` layouts
    15 | - Known architectural modules, classes, methods, and functions
    16 | - First-party import resolution
    17 | 
    18 | Run:
    19 | 
    20 | ```powershell
    21 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_repositories.py `
    22 |   --fixtures-root C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks `
    23 |   --output benchmarks\results
    24 | ```
    25 | 
    26 | Use `--repository flask` to run one fixture. Results are written as JSON and
    27 | Markdown so changes in analyzer quality can be reviewed rather than inferred
    28 | from node counts alone.
    29 | 
    30 | ## Retrieval benchmark
    31 | 
    32 | The local retrieval benchmark measures file Hit@5, Hit@10, mean reciprocal rank,
    33 | nDCG@10, indexing/restoration time, cold/warm query latency, latency percentiles, and
    34 | process peak memory against known evidence files:
    35 | 
    36 | ```powershell
    37 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval.py `
    38 |   --repository . `
    39 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-latest.json
    40 | ```
    41 | 
    42 | Add repository-specific cases by supplying another JSON file with `--cases`.
    43 | 
    44 | V3 also contains a 50-question, three-repository development benchmark with explicit
    45 | development/held-out labels, required path groups, forbidden distractors, repository and
    46 | language slices, and an adjudication gate. Pending seed labels are rejected unless the
    47 | caller explicitly opts into a non-release diagnostic:
    48 | 
    49 | ```powershell
    50 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval_v3.py `
    51 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    52 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones/pallets--flask--214023150b `
    53 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones/haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    54 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    55 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-v3.json
    56 | ```
    57 | 
    58 | See `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V3.md` for formulas, limitations, and the preserved V2-to-V3
    59 | comparison.
    60 | 
    61 | ## V4 independent-agent benchmark
    62 | 
    63 | V4 uses a separate 50-case, four-repository corpus. Each fixed endpoint independently
    64 | chooses production repository tools; candidate results, explicit source reads, and final
    65 | citations are scored separately. The benchmark also records schema corrections, retries,
    66 | tokens, latency, and trace-correlated hook/log quality.
    67 | 
    68 | ```powershell
    69 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_agentic_retrieval_v4.py `
    70 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    71 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones\pallets--flask--214023150b `
    72 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones\haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    73 |   --repository open-notebook=.waypoint-clones\lfnovo--open-notebook--5d0a28a4b0 `
    74 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-m.1:free `
    75 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free `
    76 |   --max-cases 50 `
    77 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    78 |   --confirm-live-provider-usage `
    79 |   --output benchmarks\results\agentic-v4-poolside-campaign.json
    80 | ```
    81 | 
    82 | The current execution status and non-transient OpenRouter daily-quota blocker are
    83 | documented in `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V4.md`.

    40 | def _observable_model_blocks(content: Any) -> list[Any]:
    41 |     """Converts a model response's content blocks into plain JSON-able dicts/strings for logging.
    42 | 
    43 |     Input: `content` is the `response.content` list from a provider SDK message
    44 |     (block objects that may be pydantic models, plain objects with `__dict__`, or
    45 |     already-plain values); falsy input is treated as an empty list. Called only
    46 |     from `RepositoryAgentService.answer` when logging the `model.response_received`
    47 |     event, so tool-call/text blocks are observable in logs/traces without asserting
    48 |     anything about the model's hidden reasoning process.
    49 |     """
    50 |     rendered: list[Any] = []
    51 |     for block in content or []:
    52 |         if hasattr(block, "model_dump"):
    53 |             rendered.append(block.model_dump(mode="json"))
    54 |         elif hasattr(block, "__dict__"):
    55 |             rendered.append(dict(vars(block)))
    56 |         else:
    57 |             rendered.append(str(block))
    58 |     return rendered

     2 | 
     3 | Waypoint turns Python, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS repositories into an
     4 | evidence-aware code graph and a role-specific onboarding workspace. It uses
     5 | static analysis only: analyzed repository code is never imported or executed.
     6 | 
     7 | ## Architecture
     8 | 
     9 | ```mermaid
    10 | flowchart TD
    11 |     UI[React + TypeScript UI] -->|HTTP /api/v1| API[FastAPI application]
    12 |     API --> IMPORT[Local path or secured GitHub clone]
    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]
    26 |     VALIDATE --> UI
    27 |     UI --> COMPARE[Independent two-agent comparison]
    28 |     COMPARE --> TOOLS
    29 |     MCP[MCP server: 30 tools] --> GRAPH
    30 |     MCP --> SEARCH
    31 |     HOOKS[Pre / post / error hooks and JSONL traces] -.observe.-> API
    32 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> AGENT
    33 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> TOOLS
    34 | ```
    35 | 
    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,

# How a Billing Failure Propagates End-to-End

The path from a lost API key to a final HTTP error touches five distinct layers. Here is how they connect.

---

## 1. Startup Detection — `provider_startup_probe`

When the FastAPI application starts, `backend/app/main.py` calls `model_provider_router.initialize()`. Whether that probe actually runs is controlled by the `WAYPOINT_PROVIDER_STARTUP_PROBE` environment variable, which defaults to `True`.

Inside `ModelProviderRouter.initialize()`, the router calls the configured primary provider (Anthropic API, OpenRouter, or Bedrock) with a minimal test request. If that probe call raises an exception that `is_billing_or_capacity_error()` recognises, the router immediately activates the Claude Code subscription fallback **at startup** rather than waiting for the first real request to fail.

`is_billing_or_capacity_error()` is the shared classifier used at every layer. It checks:
- HTTP status codes `{402, 429, 529}` via `getattr(exc, "status_code", None)`
- String signals in the lowercased exception message: `"credit balance"`, `"billing"`, `"payment required"`, `"purchase credits"`, `"insufficient credit"`, `"insufficient_quota"`, `"usage limit"`, `"rate limit"`, `"overloaded"`

```python
# provider.py lines 32–45
status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
message = str(exc).lower()
signals = (
    "credit balance", "billing", "payment required",
    "purchase credits", "insufficient credit",
    "insufficient_quota", "usage limit", "rate limit", "overloaded",
)
return status in {402, 429, 529} or any(signal in message for signal in signals)
```

---

## 2. Provider Fallback — `ProviderMessages.create` and `activate_claude_code`

If the billing error is **not** caught at startup (e.g. the probe was disabled, or billing was revoked mid-session), the fallback fires at the first live model call.

`ProviderMessages.create` is the single entry point for every model call in the system. In single-model mode it calls the Anthropic API directly. If that raises and `is_billing_or_capacity_error` returns `True`, it calls `router.activate_claude_code(...)` and immediately retries the same request against the Claude Code subscription:

```python
# provider.py lines 1002–1011
try:
    response = self.router._anthropic_client().messages.create(**request)
    return response
except Exception as exc:
    if not settings.claude_code_fallback or not is_billing_or_capacity_error(exc):
        raise
    self.router.activate_claude_code(
        "runtime API billing/capacity failure", exc, probe=False
    )
    return self.router._claude_code.messages.create(**request)
```

The `WAYPOINT_CLAUDE_CODE_FALLBACK` env var (default `True`) gates this. If it is `False`, the exception is re-raised immediately without any fallback.

In **dual-role mode** (`WAYPOINT_MODEL_ARCHITECTURE=dual`), `create_for_role` routes investigation and synthesis turns to independently configured provider/model endpoints, and the same `is_billing_or_capacity_error` check applies per-role.

---

## 3. Endpoint Routing — `ModelProviderRouter` and `RoutedModelClient`

`ModelProviderRouter` is a module-level singleton. Its `client()` method returns a `RoutedModelClient`, whose `.messages` is a `ProviderMessages` instance. This is the uniform facade every agent uses:

```
RepositoryAgentService._client()
  → model_provider_router.client()
  → RoutedModelClient.messages  (ProviderMessages)
  → ProviderMessages.create()
  → routes to: anthropic / openrouter / bedrock / claude-code
```

The active provider is tracked in `router.active_provider` (initially `"unavailable"`). After `initialize()` succeeds, it is set to `"anthropic"`, `"openrouter"`, `"bedrock"`, or `"claude-code"`. The `RepositoryAgentService.available` property simply reads `model_provider_router.available`, which is `True` only when `active_provider != "unavailable"`.

For **OpenRouter** specifically, the endpoint is `{settings.openrouter_base_url}/chat/completions` (default …<3730 chars truncated>

# How a Billing Failure Propagates End-to-End

The path from a lost API key to a final HTTP error touches five distinct layers. Here is how they connect.

---

## 1. Startup Detection — `provider_startup_probe`

When the FastAPI application starts, `backend/app/main.py` calls `model_provider_router.initialize()`. Whether that probe actually runs is controlled by the `WAYPOINT_PROVIDER_STARTUP_PROBE` environment variable, which defaults to `True`.

Inside `ModelProviderRouter.initialize()`, the router calls the configured primary provider (Anthropic API, OpenRouter, or Bedrock) with a minimal test request. If that probe call raises an exception that `is_billing_or_capacity_error()` recognises, the router immediately activates the Claude Code subscription fallback **at startup** rather than waiting for the first real request to fail.

`is_billing_or_capacity_error()` is the shared classifier used at every layer. It checks:
- HTTP status codes `{402, 429, 529}` via `getattr(exc, "status_code", None)`
- String signals in the lowercased exception message: `"credit balance"`, `"billing"`, `"payment required"`, `"purchase credits"`, `"insufficient credit"`, `"insufficient_quota"`, `"usage limit"`, `"rate limit"`, `"overloaded"`

```python
# provider.py lines 32–45
status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
message = str(exc).lower()
signals = (
    "credit balance", "billing", "payment required",
    "purchase credits", "insufficient credit",
    "insufficient_quota", "usage limit", "rate limit", "overloaded",
)
return status in {402, 429, 529} or any(signal in message for signal in signals)
```

---

## 2. Provider Fallback — `ProviderMessages.create` and `activate_claude_code`

If the billing error is **not** caught at startup (e.g. the probe was disabled, or billing was revoked mid-session), the fallback fires at the first live model call.

`ProviderMessages.create` is the single entry point for every model call in the system. In single-model mode it calls the Anthropic API directly. If that raises and `is_billing_or_capacity_error` returns `True`, it calls `router.activate_claude_code(...)` and immediately retries the same request against the Claude Code subscription:

```python
# provider.py lines 1002–1011
try:
    response = self.router._anthropic_client().messages.create(**request)
    return response
except Exception as exc:
    if not settings.claude_code_fallback or not is_billing_or_capacity_error(exc):
        raise
    self.router.activate_claude_code(
        "runtime API billing/capacity failure", exc, probe=False
    )
    return self.router._claude_code.messages.create(**request)
```

The `WAYPOINT_CLAUDE_CODE_FALLBACK` env var (default `True`) gates this. If it is `False`, the exception is re-raised immediately without any fallback.

In **dual-role mode** (`WAYPOINT_MODEL_ARCHITECTURE=dual`), `create_for_role` routes investigation and synthesis turns to independently configured provider/model endpoints, and the same `is_billing_or_capacity_error` check applies per-role.

  → model_provider_router.client()
  → RoutedModelClient.messages  (ProviderMessages)
  → ProviderMessages.create()
  → routes to: anthropic / openrouter / bedrock / claude-code
```

The active provider is tracked in `router.active_provider` (initially `"unavailable"`). After `initialize()` succeeds, it is set to `"anthropic"`, `"openrouter"`, `"bedrock"`, or `"claude-code"`. The `RepositoryAgentService.available` property simply reads `model_provider_router.available`, which is `True` only when `active_provider != "unavailable"`.

class ModelComparisonService:
    """Runs one question through two distinct provider/model endpoints against a single
    frozen evidence set so their answers can be benchmarked head-to-head.

    Instantiated per-request by backend/app/api/routes.py:compare_repository_answers
    (POST /analyses/{analysis_id}/answer/compare) whenever a user asks for a
    model-vs-model comparison; exists so both models are judged on identical evidence
    and identical rules rather than on separately-retrieved context.
    """

    def __init__(self, session: AnalysisSession) -> None:
        """Bind this comparison run to an analysis session and its repository search index."""
        self.session = session
        self.index = repository_indexes.get(session)

    @staticmethod
    def _endpoints() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Resolve the two (provider, model) pairs to compare, from the configured
        investigation and synthesis roles.

        Raises ValueError when dual-role model architecture is disabled, or when both
        roles resolve to the same provider/model (a comparison needs two distinct
        endpoints). Called by compare() at the start of every comparison run.
        """
        endpoints = [
            (settings.investigation_provider, settings.investigation_model),
            (settings.synthesis_provider, settings.synthesis_model),
        ]
        if not model_provider_router.dual_role_enabled:
            raise ValueError("Model comparison requires WAYPOINT_MODEL_ARCHITECTURE=dual")
        if endpoints[0] == endpoints[1]:
            raise ValueErro

class DiagnosticFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    """Dense terminal formatter optimized for correlation and grepability."""

    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        timestamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime(record.created))
        milliseconds = int(record.msecs)
        event = getattr(record, "event", "log.message")
        fields = getattr(record, "fields", {})
        prefix = (
            f"{timestamp}.{milliseconds:03d}Z "
            f"{record.levelname:<8} "
            f"event={event} "
            f"pid={record.process} process={record.processName} "
            f"thread={record.threadName}:{record.thread} "
            f"trace={getattr(record, 'trace_id', '-')} "
            f"span={getattr(record, 'span_id', '-')} "
            f"at={record.name}.{record.funcName}:{record.lineno}"
        )
        message = record.getMessage()
        rendered_fields = ""
        if fields:
            rendered_fields = " fields=" + json.dumps(
                sanitize(fields), ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, default=str
            )
        rendered = f"{prefix} message={json.dumps(message)}{rendered_fields}"
        if record.exc_info:
            rendered += "\n" + "".join(
                traceback.format_exception(*record.exc_info)
            ).rstrip()
        return rendered

    log_event(
        logger,
        logging.INFO,
        "process.startup",
        "Application process starting",
        app=settings.app_name,
        process=process_metadata(),

    except Exception as exc:
        provider = "unavailable"

            logger,
            logging.ERROR,

        logger,

def _role_score(self, node: GraphNode, role: DeveloperRole) -> float:
        name = node.qualified_name.lower()
        keyword_score = sum(
            16 for keyword in ROLE_KEYWORDS[role] if keyword in name
        )
        centrality = min(self.degree[node.id], 30) * 0.8
        support_code_penalty = (
            -35
            if role != DeveloperRole.QA
            and any(
                part in name
                for part in (
                    "test",
                    "fixture",
                    "conftest",
                    "benchmark",
                    "docs",
                    "example",
                    "script",
                )
            )
            else 0
        )
        package_depth_penalty = max(0, name.count(".") - 3) * 0.5
        return (
            keyword_score
            + centrality
            + support_code_penalty
            - package_depth_penalty
        )

def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        """Open a SQLite connection configured for concurrent-safe access.

        Creates the parent directory if needed, enables row_factory for
        dict-like row access, enforces foreign keys, and sets WAL journal mode so
        readers don't block the writer. Called at the start of every public
        method on this class via `closing(self._connect())`.
        """
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        connection = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=20)
        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        return connection

def is_billing_or_capacity_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
    """Recognize failures for which the subscription-backed fallback is useful.

    Checks the exception's optional `status_code` attribute (as set by the
    Anthropic/httpx SDKs) against {402, 429, 529} and scans `str(exc)` for known
    billing/quota/rate-limit/overload phrases. Input: any BaseException, with or
    without a `status_code` attribute. Called by ProviderMessages.create,
    ModelProviderRouter.create_for_role, and ModelProviderRouter.initialize to
    decide whether a failed request should fall back to the Claude Code
    subscription instead of raising; exercised directly in
    backend/tests/test_provider.py.
    """
    status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
    message = str(exc).lower()
    signals = (
        "credit balance",
        "billing",
        "payment required",
        "purchase credits",
        "insufficient credit",
        "insufficient_quota",
        "usage limit",
        "rate limit",
        "overloaded",
    )
    return status in {402, 429, 529} or any(signal in message for signal in signals)

class DiagnosticFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    """Dense terminal formatter optimized for correlation and grepability."""

    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        timestamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime(record.created))
        milliseconds = int(record.msecs)
        event = getattr(record, "event", "log.message")
        fields = getattr(record, "fields", {})
        prefix = (
            f"{timestamp}.{milliseconds:03d}Z "
            f"{record.levelname:<8} "
            f"event={event} "
            f"pid={record.process} process={record.processName} "
            f"thread={record.threadName}:{record.thread} "
            f"trace={getattr(record, 'trace_id', '-')} "
            f"span={getattr(record, 'span_id', '-')} "
            f"at={record.name}.{record.funcName}:{record.lineno}"
        )
        message = record.getMessage()
        rendered_fields = ""
        if fields:
            rendered_fields = " fields=" + json.dumps(
                sanitize(fields), ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, default=str
            )
        rendered = f"{prefix} message={json.dumps(message)}{rendered_fields}"
        if record.exc_info:
            rendered += "\n" + "".join(
                traceback.format_exception(*record.exc_info)
            ).rstrip()
        return rendered

        name = node.qualified_name.lower()

            16 for keyword in ROLE_KEYWORDS[role] if keyword in name
        )
        centrality = min(self.degree[node.id], 30) * 0.8
        support_code_penalty = (
            -35
            if role != DeveloperRole.QA
            and any(
                part in name
                for part in (
                    "test",
                    "fixture",
                    "conftest",
                    "benchmark",
                    "docs",
                    "example",
                    "script",
                )
            )
            else 0
        )
        package_depth_penalty = max(0, name.count(".") - 3) * 0.5
        return (
            keyword_score
            + centrality
            + support_code_penalty
            - package_depth_penalty
        )

        from ctypes import wintypes

        get_current_process = ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetCurrentProcess
        get_current_process.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
        get_process_memory_info = ctypes.windll.psapi.GetProcessMemoryInfo
        get_process_memory_info.argtypes = [

        counters = ProcessMemoryCounters()

            process, ctypes.byref(counters), counters.cb
        )
        return (

def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        """Open a SQLite connection configured for concurrent-safe access.

        Creates the parent directory if needed, enables row_factory for
        dict-like row access, enforces foreign keys, and sets WAL journal mode so
        readers don't block the writer. Called at the start of every public
        method on this class via `closing(self._connect())`.
        """
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        connection = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=20)
        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        return connection

# Token usage and metering

## What Waypoint currently controls

Waypoint manages token usage through hard output limits and indirect input-context
bounds.

### Hard model and loop limits

- `WAYPOINT_AGENT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, default 6,000 and clamped to 512-32,000, limits
  the maximum generated tokens for primary agent calls.
- Assessment calls use a smaller fixed 1,800-token output limit.
- The API startup probe uses only eight maximum output tokens.
- The Claude Code health probe asks for at most 32 output tokens.
- `WAYPOINT_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`, default eight, stops the outer evidence loop.
- `WAYPOINT_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TURNS`, default four, bounds SDK-internal turns needed to
  produce one structured Waypoint action batch.
- The Claude Code structured action schema permits at most six action calls in one
  batch.
- Final rounds force the appropriate submission tool once evidence exists, reducing
  indefinite browsing.

### Input-context controls

- Chat memory retains the most recent `WAYPOINT_CHAT_HISTORY_TURNS` user/assistant
  turns, default 12 and clamped to 1-50.
- Repository search returns at most 50 chunks to an agent request.
- `read_source` returns at most 250 lines per call.
- Tree listings, graph depth, feature candidates, entry points, related tests,
  diagnostics, and dependency impact all have explicit bounds.
- The agent receives selected chunks and tool results rather than the entire repository.
- Tool descriptions steer broad questions to high-yield semantic tools, reducing
  repeated generic search.
- Independent tools can run in one round, reducin

## 10. Current limitations and honest boundaries

- Static parsing cannot prove runtime dispatch, reflection, dependency injection, dynamic imports, generated code, or data-dependent calls. Such relationships should remain possible/unresolved rather than definite.
- The local sparse vectorizer supports fuzzy lexical similarity, but it is not equivalent to a learned neural code embedding model.
- Conversation memory is a bounded transcript, not semantic long-term memory or user-model personalization.
- HTML and CSS are parsed and indexed, but their relationship extraction is necessarily shallower than Python/Java/JS/TS application semantics.
- The runtime agents use tools and specialized workflows, not a literal `SKILL.md` skill package.
- Dual-model capability is configurable, but it only operates as a two-role system when `WAYPOINT_MODEL_ARCHITECTURE` is explicitly set to a dual value and both chosen endpoints are usable.
- Retry loops are intentionally bounded. Exhaustion produces an error instead of silently accepting invalid or unsupported output.

        self,

        """Switch the active provider to the Claude Code subscription fallback.

        Input: reason - human-readable string logged with the switch; exc - the
        exception that triggered the fallback, if any; probe - set False to skip
        `_probe_claude_code`'s health check when the switch must apply immediately

        unavailable or fails; also patched directly in
        backend/tests/test_provider.py to assert fallback behavior.

def is_billing_or_capacity_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
    """Recognize failures for which the subscription-backed fallback is useful.

    Checks the exception's optional `status_code` attribute (as set by the
    Anthropic/httpx SDKs) against {402, 429, 529} and scans `str(exc)` for known
    billing/quota/rate-limit/overload phrases. Input: any BaseException, with or
    without a `status_code` attribute. Called by ProviderMessages.create,
    ModelProviderRouter.create_for_role, and ModelProviderRouter.initialize to
    decide whether a failed request should fall back to the Claude Code
    subscription instead of raising; exercised directly in
    backend/tests/test_provider.py.
    """
    status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
    message = str(exc).lower()
    signals = (
        "credit balance",
        "billing",
        "payment required",
        "purchase credits",
        "insufficient credit",
        "insufficient_quota",
        "usage limit",
        "rate limit",
        "overloaded",
    )
    return status in {402, 429, 529} or any(signal in message for signal in signals)

def _execute_tool(
        self,
        name: str,
        arguments: dict[str, Any],
        inspected: list[InspectedSpan],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate model input, execute the server tool, then validate its result.

        Model mistakes raise ``ToolInputValidationError`` and are safe to return as
        bounded correction feedback. A ``ToolOutputValidationError`` means Waypoint
        violated its own server-side contract and is deliberately classified as a
        non-retryable application defect.
        """
        contract = TOOL_CONTRACTS.get(name)
        if contract is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown repository tool: {name}")
        validated = contract.validate_input(arguments)
        raw_result = self._dispatch_tool(
            name,
            validated.model_dump(mode="python"),
            inspected,
        )
        return contract.validate_output(raw_result)

# Waypoint V4 - validated agents and independent retrieval evaluation

Date: 2026-07-27

## Outcome

V4 changes the evaluation boundary. V3 measures Waypoint's deterministic retrieval
engine. The older comparison measures synthesis over one frozen evidence bundle. V4
instead measures which model retrieves better when each model must independently choose
and call the same production Waypoint tools.

The complete 50-case Poolside campaign is currently **blocked**, not passed or failed.
Both selected endpoints exhausted the OpenRouter account's daily free-model quota before
a scored run completed. The failure artifact is retained and described below; it is not
converted into a retrieval-quality score.

## Production changes exercised by V4

### Strict tool contracts

`backend/app/agent/tool_contracts.py` is the source of truth for all 17 repository tools.
Each contract has:

- a strict Pydantic input model with forbidden extra fields, primitive-type enforcement,
  bounds, enums, and cross-field validation;
- provider JSON Schema generated from the same input model;
- a Pydantic output model for the server-owned result;
- distinct failures for invalid model input and invalid Waypoint output.

Invalid model input returns a machine-readable correction envelope. Tool-input
corrections and final-submission corrections have independent default budgets of two.
Both operate inside the eight-round outer agent limit; they do not multiply it.

Ask validates `submit_answer`, verifies citations are in evidence exposed during that
run, performs at most one bounded evidence recovery read whe

| symbol/module chunk | up to about 160 lines | stops giant modules dominating retrieval |
| non-symbol/context chunk | 120 lines, stride 100 (20-line overlap) | preserves boundary context |
| direct source read | at most 250 lines per call | bounded tool output |
| tree listing | implementation cap 5,000 paths | bounded discovery output |
| search result limit | internal retrieval/tool-specific caps; model comparison 2-15 evidence items | controls prompt evidence volume |
| Ask/onboarding question | 2-500 characters | bounded prompt input |
| supplied request history | at most 10 messages | caller-provided memory bound |
| stored chat context | 12 turns by default, configurable 1-50 | persistent recent-memory window |
| agent tool rounds | 8 by default, configurable 1-20 | stops unbounded agent loops |
| Claude Code turns | 8 by default, hard range 1-8 | SDK execution bound |
| investigation rounds | 3 by default, hard range 1-10 | task-role bound |
| synthesis attempts | 2 by default, hard range 1-5 | validation retry bound |
| generated output request | 6,000 tokens by default, range 512-32,000 | provider output budget |
| final Ask answer | 1-30,000 characters | schema output guard |
| answer basis | 1-2,000 characters | concise provenance |
| answer citations | at most 30 | response/UX bound |
| suggested follow-ups | at most 5 | response bound |
| citation relevance | at most 500 characters | response bound |
| onboarding duration | 5-120 minutes | product route bound |
| onboarding steps | 2-10 | route-size guard |
| files per onboarding step | 1-8 | cognitive/input

Relevant implementation:

- `backend/app/config.py:68-80` and `backend/app/config.py:147-182` — architecture, endpoints, and defaults.
- `backend/app/agent/provider.py:390-457` — role routing and provider fallback.
- `backend/app/agent/service.py:646-711` — role transition and tool restrictions.

### 7.2 Feature split

At the product level, the primary AI capability is grounded repository understanding: Ask plus role/objective-specific onboarding routes. Secondary AI capabilities build on the same evidence layer:

- safe first-contribution missions;
- repository issue synthesis;
- assessments of onboarding comprehension;
- cross-model comparison/benchmarking.

These are not separate parsers or separate RAG systems. They reuse the same graph, chunks, retrieval index, memory conventions, and source validation while changing the prompt, final schema, and workflow-specific checks.

## 8. Output validation and retry loops

Waypoint uses several validation layers rather than trusting model prose directly.

### 8.1 Tool input constraints

Tool schemas bound lists, strings, result counts, graph depth, line ranges, and enum values, and generally reject unknown properties. These constraints reduce malformed calls before application dispatch.

Ask output must validate as `SubmittedAnswer`.     `model_provider_router`), validates the model's final `submit_answer` citations

    and call its `_client`/`_execute_tool` helpers directly to run their own,
    differently-prompted tool loops without duplicating tool dispatch or provider
    setup).

        analysis. Called at the top of every route/agent that needs repository-agent

        self,
        name: str,
        arguments: dict[str, Any],
        inspected: list[InspectedSpan],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate model input, execute the server tool, then validate its result.

        Model mistakes raise ``ToolInputValidationError`` and are safe to return as
        bounded correction feedback. A ``ToolOutputValidationError`` means Waypoint
        violated its own server-side contract and is deliberately classified as a
        non-retryable application defect.

        contract = TOOL_CONTRACTS.get(name)

        validated = contract.validate_input(arguments)
        raw_result = self._dispatch_tool(
            name,
            validated.model_dump(mode="python"),
            inspected,
        )

and call the same production Waypoint tools.

At the product level, the primary AI capability is grounded repository understanding: Ask plus role/objective-specific onboarding routes. Secondary AI capabilities build on the same evidence layer:

def _read_source(
    session: AnalysisSession,
    source_path: str,
    canonical_path: str | None = None,
) -> SourceDocument:
    """Reads one indexed source file's text off disk, guarding against path traversal.

    Input: an AnalysisSession, the raw path the caller asked for, and an optional
    canonical/resolved path (as produced by the repository index) when it differs
    from the requested path. Rejects paths that are not in session.source_paths or
    that resolve outside session.root. Used by get_source (GET
    /api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/source) and directly unit-tested in
    backend/tests/test_questions.py; this is the guarded file read behind the
    "view this file" code viewer, so it must never escape the cloned/allowed repo root.
    """
    normalized = Path(source_path).as_posix().lstrip("/")
    canonical = Path(canonical_path or normalized).as_posix().lstrip("/")
    if canonical not in session.source_paths:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source file was not found")
    candidate = (session.root / canonical).resolve()
    try:
        candidate.relative_to(session.root.resolve())
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source file was not found") from exc
    try:
        content = candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source file could not be read") from exc
    return SourceDocument(
        analysis_id=session.id,
        path=normalized,
        language=_source_language(candidate)

    canonical = Path(canonical_path or normalized).as_posix().lstrip("/")
    if canonical not in session.source_paths:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source file was not found")
    candidate = (session.root / canonical).resolve()
    try:
        candidate.relative_to(session.root.resolve())
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source file was not found") from exc
    try:
        content = candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source file could not be read") from exc
    return SourceDocument(
        analysis_id=session.id,
        path=normalized,
        language=_source_language(candidate)

async def analyze_github_repository(request: GitHubAnalysisRequest) -> AnalysisReport:
    """Shallow-clones a public GitHub repository and analyzes it.

    HTTP entry point: POST /api/v1/analysis/github with a GitHubAnalysisRequest
    body ({"repository_url": str}, pre-validated by validate_repository_url).
    Delegates cloning to github_cloner.clone (GitHubRepositoryCloner in
    backend/app/repository_import.py) and analysis to _analyze, both in a
    threadpool; maps invalid URLs/unavailable git/clone failures to 422/503/400.
    Called by frontend/src/api.ts analyzeGitHubRepository(); this is the entry
    point for the "analyze a GitHub repo" onboarding flow.
    """
    identity = parse_github_repository(request.repository_url)
    try:
        root = await run_in_threadpool(github_cloner.clone, request.repository_url)
        return await run_in_threadpool(_analyze, root, identity.name)
    except InvalidGitHubRepository as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=str(exc)) from exc
    except GitUnavailableError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc
    except (GitCloneError, RepositoryImportError) as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc

async def analyze_repository(request: AnalysisRequest) -> AnalysisReport:
    """Analyzes a local repository already present on disk and creates an analysis session.

    HTTP entry point: POST /api/v1/analysis with an AnalysisRequest body
    ({"repository_path": str}). Resolves the path (rejecting it with 403 if it
    escapes settings.allowed_root) and delegates to _analyze in a threadpool,
    which itself uses RepositoryAnalyzer (backend/app/graph/analyzer.py). Called
    by frontend/src/api.ts analyzeRepository(); this is the entry point for the
    "analyze a local repo" flow that seeds the analysis_id every other endpoint uses.
    """
    requested = Path(request.repository_path).expanduser()
    resolved = requested.resolve() if requested.is_absolute() else (settings.allowed_root / requested).resolve()
    try:
        # relative_to raises ValueError if resolved is not inside allowed_root, catching ../ escapes
        resolved.relative_to(settings.allowed_root)
    except ValueError as exc:
        log_event(logger, logging.WARNING, "security.repository_path_rejected", "Repository path rejected because it escapes the configured root", requested_path=request.repository_path, resolved_path=resolved, allowed_root=settings.allowed_root)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Repository path is outside the configured allowed root") from exc
    try:
        return await run_in_threadpool(_analyze, resolved)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(exc)) from exc

async def answer_repository_question(analysis_id: str, request: GroundedQuestion) -> GroundedAnswer:
    """Answers a free-form natural-language question about the repository with cited evidence.

    HTTP entry point: POST /api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/answer, path param
    analysis_id plus a GroundedQuestion body (question, history,
    conversation_id, etc.). Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to be configured (503 if
    not); delegates to RepositoryAgentService(session).answer
    (backend/app/agent/service.py). Called by frontend/src/api.ts
    askRepository(); this is the main "ask the codebase" chat/Q&A endpoint.
    """
    service = RepositoryAgentService(_session(analysis_id))
    if not service.available:
        # 503 (not 500) signals a missing/optional dependency (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) rather than a server error
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=503,
            detail="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required for AI-generated repository answers",
        )
    try:
        return await run_in_threadpool(service.answer, request)
    except (AgentUnavailableError, AgentExecutionError) as exc:
        raise _agent_error(exc) from exc
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc

async def compare_repository_answers(
    analysis_id: str,
    request: ModelComparisonRequest,
) -> ModelComparisonReport:
    """Sends one question and one frozen evidence bundle to both configured models.

    HTTP entry point: POST /api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/answer/compare, path
    param analysis_id plus a ModelComparisonRequest body. Delegates to
    ModelComparisonService(session).compare (backend/app/agent/comparison.py)
    in a threadpool. Not currently called by the main frontend UI; used by
    evaluation tooling in verification/scripts/model_comparison_benchmark.py
    and model_quality_benchmark.py to compare answer quality across model
    providers on identical evidence.
    """
    try:
        return await run_in_threadpool(
            ModelComparisonService(_session(analysis_id)).compare,
            request,
        )
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc
    except Exception as exc:
        raise _agent_error(exc) from exc

1 | # Waypoint — Adaptive Codebase Onboarding
     2 | 
     3 | Waypoint turns Python, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS repositories into an
     4 | evidence-aware code graph and a role-specific onboarding workspace. It uses
     5 | static analysis only: analyzed repository code is never imported or executed.
     6 | 
     7 | ## Architecture
     8 | 
     9 | ```mermaid
    10 | flowchart TD
    11 |     UI[React + TypeScript UI] -->|HTTP /api/v1| API[FastAPI application]
    12 |     API --> IMPORT[Local path or secured GitHub clone]
    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]
    26 |     VALIDATE --> UI
    27 |     UI --> COMPARE[Independent two-agent comparison]
    28 |     COMPARE --> TOOLS
    29 |     MCP[MCP server: 30 tools] --> GRAPH
    30 |     MCP --> SEARCH
    31 |     HOOKS[Pre / post / error hooks and JSONL traces] -.observe.-> API
    32 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> AGENT
    33 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> TOOLS
    34 | ```
    35 | 
    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,
    39 | chunks, lexical/vector indexes, issues, and conversation memory. The model layer supports
    40 | OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, and the Claude Agent SDK. In dual mode a low-cost model can
    41 | investigate through tools while a stronger model synthesizes a validated answer.

    62 | - local subword-vector retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion, graph expansion, index

    64 | - pre/post/error function hooks, correlated model/tool/retrieval traces, rotating JSONL
    65 |   diagnostics, and a 30-tool MCP connector over stdio or Streamable HTTP
    66 | - readable GitHub-flavored Markdown rendering …<1000 chars truncated>

1 | # External repository benchmarks
     2 | 
     3 | This suite validates the analyzer against shallow clones of established Python
     4 | repositories. Clones live outside the application workspace by default at
     5 | `C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks`.
     6 | 
     7 | The benchmark verifies:
     8 | 
     9 | - Parse success and performance
    10 | - Unique, stable node and edge identities
    11 | - Valid graph endpoints
    12 | - Valid source spans
    13 | - Evidence-status invariants
    14 | - Correct package names for flat and `src/` layouts
    15 | - Known architectural modules, classes, methods, and functions
    16 | - First-party import resolution
    17 | 
    18 | Run:
    19 | 
    20 | ```powershell
    21 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_repositories.py `
    22 |   --fixtures-root C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks `
    23 |   --output benchmarks\results
    24 | ```
    25 | 
    26 | Use `--repository flask` to run one fixture. Results are written as JSON and
    27 | Markdown so changes in analyzer quality can be reviewed rather than inferred
    28 | from node counts alone.
    29 | 
    30 | ## Retrieval benchmark
    31 | 
    32 | The local retrieval benchmark measures file Hit@5, Hit@10, mean reciprocal rank,
    33 | nDCG@10, indexing/restoration time, cold/warm query latency, latency percentiles, and
    34 | process peak memory against known evidence files:
    35 | 
    36 | ```powershell
    37 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval.py `
    38 |   --repository . `
    39 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-latest.json
    40 | ```
    41 | 
    42 | Add repository-specific cases by supplying another JSON file with `--cases`.
    43 | 
    44 | V3 also contains a 50-question, three-repository development benchmark with explicit
    45 | development/held-out labels, required path groups, forbidden distractors, repository and
    46 | language slices, and an adjudication gate. Pending seed labels are rejected unless the
    47 | caller explicitly opts into a non-release diagnostic:
    48 | 
    49 | ```powershell
    50 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval_v3.py `
    51 |   --repository waypoint=. `

    53 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones/haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    54 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    55 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-v3.json
    56 | ```
    57 | 
    58 | See `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V3.md` for formulas, limitations, and the preserved V2-to-V3
    59 | comparison.

    61 | ## V4 independent-agent benchmark

    63 | V4 uses a separate 50-case, four-repository corpus. Each fixed endpoint independently
    64 | chooses production repository tools; candidate results, explicit source reads, and final
    65 | citations are scored separately. The benchmark also records schema corrections, retries,

    73 |   --repository open-notebook=.waypoint-clones\lfnovo--open-notebook--5d0a28a4b0 `
    74 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-m.1:free `
    75 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free `

    77 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    78 |   --confirm-live-provider-usage `

    80 | ```
    81 | 
    82 | The current execution status and non-transient OpenRouter daily-quota blocker are

# How a Repository Tool Request Flows Through Argument Validation, Execution, Result Validation, and Correction Feedback

This is the complete lifecycle for every tool call the model makes during a `RepositoryAgentService.answer` investigation round. Four distinct stages are involved, each with its own Pydantic model and error path.

---

## Stage 1 — Argument Validation (`ToolContract.validate_input`)

Every tool is registered in `TOOL_CONTRACTS`, a dict that maps tool names to `ToolContract` dataclass instances. Each contract pairs a tool name with a Pydantic **input model** (e.g. `SearchInput`, `ReadSourceInput`) and a Pydantic **output model** (e.g. `SearchOutput`, `ReadSourceOutput`).

```python
# backend/app/agent/tool_contracts.py  lines 184–200
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ToolContract:
    name: str
    description: str
    input_model: type[BaseModel]
    output_model: type[BaseModel]

    def validate_input(self, value: Any) -> BaseModel:
        try:
            return self.input_model.model_validate(value, strict=True)
        except ValidationError as exc:
            raise ToolInputValidationError(self.name, exc) from exc
```

All input models inherit from `ContractModel`, which sets `extra="forbid"` and `strict=True` — unknown fields and implicit type coercions are both rejected. Cross-field rules are enforced with `@model_validator`; for example, `ReadSourceInput` rejects any call where `end_line < start_line`, and `RelatedTestsInput` requires at least one of `query` or `node_id`.

When validation fails, a `ToolInputValidationError` is raised, carrying the tool name and the structured Pydantic error list (URLs and context stripped for cleanliness).

---

## Stage 2 — Execution (`_execute_tool` inside `execute_tool`)

Inside `answer`, each non-`submit_answer` tool call is dispatched through the inner `execute_tool` closure, which is submitted to a `ThreadPoolExecutor` so independent tool calls in one round run concurrently. The closure calls `self._execute_tool(name, arguments, local_inspected)`, which looks up the contract, validates the input, dispatches to the matching `SemanticRepositoryTools` or retrieval-index method, and returns a plain dict result.

```python
# backend/app/agent/service.py  lines 1188–1192
result = self._execute_tool(name, arguments, local_inspected)
self._register_result_evidence(result, local_inspected)
result_paths = self._result_paths(result)
serialized = json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
```

Any `KeyError`, `TypeError`, or `ValueError` raised during execution (including `ToolInputValidationError`, which is a `ValueError` subclass) is caught by `execute_tool` and converted into an `is_error` tool-result message sent back to the model rather than aborting the whole round.

---

## Stage 3 — Result Validation (`ToolContract.validate_output`)

After execution, the raw dict result is passed through the contract's output validator:

```python
# backend/app/agent/tool_contracts.py  lines 202–207
def validate_output(self, value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        parsed = self.output_model.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise ToolOutputValidationError(self.name, exc) from exc

# How a Repository Tool Request Flows Through Argument Validation, Execution, Result Validation, and Correction Feedback

This is the complete lifecycle for every tool call the model makes during a `RepositoryAgentService.answer` investigation round. Four distinct stages are involved, each with its own Pydantic model and error path.

---

## Stage 1 — Argument Validation (`ToolContract.validate_input`)

Every tool is registered in `TOOL_CONTRACTS`, a dict that maps tool names to `ToolContract` dataclass instances. Each contract pairs a tool name with a Pydantic **input model** (e.g. `SearchInput`, `ReadSourceInput`) and a Pydantic **output model** (e.g. `SearchOutput`, `ReadSourceOutput`).

```python
# backend/app/agent/tool_contracts.py  lines 184–200
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ToolContract:
    name: str
    description: str
    input_model: type[BaseModel]
    output_model: type[BaseModel]

    def validate_input(self, value: Any) -> BaseModel:
        try:
            return self.input_model.model_validate(value, strict=True)
        except ValidationError as exc:
            raise ToolInputValidationError(self.name, exc) from exc
```

All input models inherit from `ContractModel`, which sets `extra="forbid"` and `strict=True` — unknown fields and implicit type coercions are both rejected. Cross-field rules are enforced with `@model_validator`; for example, `ReadSourceInput` rejects any call where `end_line < start_line`, and `RelatedTestsInput` requires at least one of `query` or `node_id`.

When validation fails, a `ToolInputValidationError` is raised, carrying the tool name and the structured Pydantic error list (URLs and context stripped for cleanliness).

---

## Stage 2 — Execution (`_execute_tool` inside `execute_tool`)

Inside `answer`, each non-`submit_answer` tool call is dispatched through the inner `execute_tool` closure, which is submitted to a `ThreadPoolExecutor` so independent tool calls in one round run concurrently. The closure calls `self._execute_tool(name, arguments, local_inspected)`, which looks up the contract, validates the input, dispatches to the matching `SemanticRepositoryTools` or retrieval-index method, and returns a plain dict result.

```python
# backend/app/agent/service.py  lines 1188–1192
result = self._execute_tool(name, arguments, local_inspected)
self._register_result_evidence(result, local_inspected)
result_paths = self._result_paths(result)
serialized = json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
```

After execution, the raw dict result is passed through the contract's output validator:

def validate_output(self, value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:

        parsed = self.output_model.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise ToolOutputValidationError(self.name, exc) from exc
    return parsed.model_dump(mode="json")
```

1 | # Waypoint — Adaptive Codebase Onboarding
     2 | 
     3 | Waypoint turns Python, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS repositories into an
     4 | evidence-aware code graph and a role-specific onboarding workspace. It uses
     5 | static analysis only: analyzed repository code is never imported or executed.
     6 | 
     7 | ## Architecture
     8 | 
     9 | ```mermaid
    10 | flowchart TD
    11 |     UI[React + TypeScript UI] -->|HTTP /api/v1| API[FastAPI application]
    12 |     API --> IMPORT[Local path or secured GitHub clone]
    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]
    26 |     VALIDATE --> UI
    27 |     UI --> COMPARE[Independent two-agent comparison]
    28 |     COMPARE --> TOOLS
    29 |     MCP[MCP server: 30 tools] --> GRAPH
    30 |     MCP --> SEARCH
    31 |     HOOKS[Pre / post / error hooks and JSONL traces] -.observe.-> API
    32 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> AGENT
    33 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> TOOLS
    34 | ```
    35 | 
    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,
    39 | chunks, lexical/vector indexes, issues, and conversation memory. The model layer supports
    40 | OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, and the Claude Agent SDK. In dual mode a low-cost model can
    41 | investigate through tools while a stronger model synthesizes a validated answer.
    42 | 
    43 | The detailed verification package, including coverage, Flask HTTP E2E, live multi-step
    44 | agent evidence, and same-question two-model comparison, is in
    45 | [`verification/README.md`](verification/README.md). Significant AI-assisted engineering
    46 | interactions are recorded in [`prompts.md`](prompts.md).
    47 | 
    48 | ## What is included
    49 | 
    50 | - Python AST extraction for modules, classes, functions, methods, imports, and calls
    51 | - Tree-sitter extraction for JavaScript/JSX, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS
    52 | - ES module imports/re-exports, CommonJS `require`, Java packages/imports, lexical
    53 |   containment, and conservatively inferred calls
    54 | - Explicit class-instantiation edges plus locally constructed receiver resolution for
    55 |   cross-file Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Java method calls
    56 | - Exact source spans, confidence, and unresolved-reference diagnostics
    57 | - Scalable React Flow visualization with on-demand neighborhood expansion
    58 | - Read-only Monaco source viewer and evidence inspector
    59 | - Claude-powered repository Q&A with bounded retrieval tools and validated citations
    60 | - revision-aware SQLite code indexing with persisted chunks, symbols, edges, file
    61 |   hashes, FTS5/BM25 search, and automatic refresh when repository contents change
    62 | - local subword-vector retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion, graph expansion, index
    63 |   status/rebuild controls, and restart-safe issue/onboarding state
    64 | - pre/post/error function hooks, correlated model/tool/retrieval traces, rotating JSONL
    65 |   diagnostics, and a 30-tool MCP connector over stdio or Streamable HTTP
    66 | - readable GitHub-flavored Markdown rendering …<1000 chars truncated>

1 | # External repository benchmarks
     2 | 
     3 | This suite validates the analyzer against shallow clones of established Python
     4 | repositories. Clones live outside the application workspace by default at
     5 | `C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks`.
     6 | 
     7 | The benchmark verifies:
     8 | 
     9 | - Parse success and performance
    10 | - Unique, stable node and edge identities
    11 | - Valid graph endpoints
    12 | - Valid source spans
    13 | - Evidence-status invariants
    14 | - Correct package names for flat and `src/` layouts
    15 | - Known architectural modules, classes, methods, and functions
    16 | - First-party import resolution
    17 | 
    18 | Run:
    19 | 
    20 | ```powershell
    21 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_repositories.py `
    22 |   --fixtures-root C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks `
    23 |   --output benchmarks\results
    24 | ```
    25 | 
    26 | Use `--repository flask` to run one fixture. Results are written as JSON and
    27 | Markdown so changes in analyzer quality can be reviewed rather than inferred
    28 | from node counts alone.
    29 | 
    30 | ## Retrieval benchmark
    31 | 
    32 | The local retrieval benchmark measures file Hit@5, Hit@10, mean reciprocal rank,
    33 | nDCG@10, indexing/restoration time, cold/warm query latency, latency percentiles, and
    34 | process peak memory against known evidence files:
    35 | 
    36 | ```powershell
    37 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval.py `
    38 |   --repository . `
    39 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-latest.json
    40 | ```
    41 | 
    42 | Add repository-specific cases by supplying another JSON file with `--cases`.
    43 | 
    44 | V3 also contains a 50-question, three-repository development benchmark with explicit
    45 | development/held-out labels, required path groups, forbidden distractors, repository and
    46 | language slices, and an adjudication gate. Pending seed labels are rejected unless the
    47 | caller explicitly opts into a non-release diagnostic:
    48 | 
    49 | ```powershell
    50 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval_v3.py `
    51 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    52 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones/pallets--flask--214023150b `
    53 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones/haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    54 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    55 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-v3.json
    56 | ```
    57 | 
    58 | See `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V3.md` for formulas, limitations, and the preserved V2-to-V3
    59 | comparison.
    60 | 
    61 | ## V4 independent-agent benchmark
    62 | 
    63 | V4 uses a separate 50-case, four-repository corpus. Each fixed endpoint independently
    64 | chooses production repository tools; candidate results, explicit source reads, and final
    65 | citations are scored separately. The benchmark also records schema corrections, retries,
    66 | tokens, latency, and trace-correlated hook/log quality.
    67 | 
    68 | ```powershell
    69 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_agentic_retrieval_v4.py `
    70 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    71 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones\pallets--flask--214023150b `
    72 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones\haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    73 |   --repository open-notebook=.waypoint-clones\lfnovo--open-notebook--5d0a28a4b0 `
    74 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-m.1:free `
    75 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free `
    76 |   --max-cases 50 `
    77 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    78 |   --confirm-live-provider-usage `
    79 |   --output benchmarks\results\agentic-v4-poolside-campaign.json
    80 | ```
    81 | 
    82 | The current execution status and non-transient OpenRouter daily-quota blocker are
    83 | documented in `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V4.md`.

# How a Follow-Up Question Assembles Context Before the Model Is Called

When `POST /analyses/{id}/answer` arrives with a `conversation_id` already set, `RepositoryAgentService.answer` runs through four distinct stages before it ever calls the model. Here is each stage in order.

---

## 1. Conversation Resolution and Repository Isolation

```python
conversation = conversations.get_or_create(
    self.session.id,
    request.conversation_id,
    request.conversation_scope,
)
```

`ConversationStore.get_or_create` looks up the supplied `conversation_id` in SQLite. Before returning it, the store checks **two hard isolation invariants**:

```python
if row is not None and row["analysis_id"] != analysis_id:
    raise ValueError("Conversation belongs to another analysis")
if row is not None and row["channel"] != channel:
    raise ValueError("Conversation belongs to another workspace")
```

If the stored conversation belongs to a different `analysis_id` (i.e., a different repository) or a different channel (`"ask"`, `"onboarding"`, `"inspector"`), the call raises immediately. This prevents any cross-repository or cross-workspace history leakage — a conversation thread is permanently bound to exactly one repository analysis and one UI channel.

---

## 2. Recent-Turn Window (Verbatim History)

Inside `hybrid_history`, the store first fetches the most recent `settings.chat_history_turns * 2` message rows (user + assistant interleaved) in chronological order:

```python
recent_rows = connection.execute(
    "SELECT id, role, content FROM ("
    "SELECT id, role, content FROM conversation_messages "
    "WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?"
    ") ORDER BY id ASC",
    (conversation.id, settings.chat_history_turns * 2),
).fetchall()
```

These rows are returned verbatim as `{"role": ..., "content": ...}` dicts. They form the **tail** of the assembled message list — the most recent context the model always sees in full.

---

## 3. Semantic Retrieval of Older Turns

For turns that fall outside the recent window, `hybrid_history` queries the `conversation_memories` table, which stores a **sparse subword vector** for every past turn (written by `append_turn` using `LocalCodeVectorizer.vectorize`). Each candidate is scored with a weighted formula:

```python
score = similarity * 0.85 + recency * 0.10 + (0.05 if same_revision else 0.0)
```

- **85 % — cosine similarity** between the current question's vector and the stored turn's combined `"User question: … Assistant answer: …"` vector.
- **10 % — logarithmic recency** (`1 / (1 + log1p(age_days))`), so older turns are penalised but not excluded.
- **5 % — revision bonus** if the stored turn was answered against the same repository content fingerprint as the current request.

Candidates below `settings.chat_memory_min_similarity` are dropped. The survivors are sorted by score, then greedily selected until either `settings.chat_semantic_memory_items` turns or `settings.chat_memory_max_characters` total characters are consumed. The selected turns are re-sorted by their original row ID (chronological order) and prepended **before** the recent window.

---

After the model returns a validated answer, `append_turn` writes both the user and assistant messages to `conversation_messages`, then immediately embeds the combined text into `conversation_memories`:

```python
memory_text = f"User question: {question}\nAssistant answer: {answer}"
vector = LocalCodeVectorizer.vectorize(memory_text)
connection.execute(
    "INSERT INTO conversation_memories(...) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
    (..., json.dumps(vector, ...), "local-subword-hash-v1", revision_fingerprint, ...),
)
```

The `revision_fingerprint` is stored alongside the vector so future scoring can award the same-revision bonus. class RepositoryOnboardingAgent:
    """Generates AI-driven, source-grounded onboarding experiences for a repository:
    guided reading tours, a first-contribution mission, and comprehension grading.

    Instantiated per-request by backend/app/api/routes.py for POST .../tour,
    POST .../mission, and POST .../tours/{tour_id}/answers whenever a repository
    analysis has agent access available; falls back to the non-AI
    backend/app/onboarding/service.py:OnboardingService otherwise. Exists to turn a
    fresh clone into a role- and experience-tailored learning path instead of leaving a
    new contributor to explore blind.
    """

    def __init__(self, session: AnalysisSession) -> None:
        """Bind this agent to an analysis session and wrap it in a RepositoryAgentService
        for tool execution (source/graph search) and model access."""
        self.session = session
        self.repository_agent = RepositoryAgentService(session)

    def _validated_tour(
        self,
        request: TourRequest,
        raw: dict[str, Any],
        inspected: list[InspectedSpan],
        provider: str | None = None,
    ) -> TourPlan:
        """Validate a raw submit_onboarding_tour payload and assemble it into a TourPlan,
        rejecting any step whose evidence was not actually inspected.

        Input: request is the original TourRequest (role/goal/experience/minutes); raw is
        the tool_use.input dict from the model's submission; inspected is the spans read
        so far this run; provider is the model's reported provider label, stored on the
        plan for di

def _recover_tour_evidence(
        self,
        raw: dict[str, Any],
        inspected: list[InspectedSpan],
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Safely read proposed tour ranges before one deterministic revalidation.

        A synthesis model can select a valid file from repository metadata even when the
        investigation model inspected a narrower range. We do not accept that citation
        on trust: the backend reads it through the bounded source index first.

        Input: raw is the same submit_onboarding_tour payload that just failed
        _validated_tour()'s "was not inspected" check; inspected is mutated in place with
        each newly-read span so a follow-up _validated_tour() call can succeed. Caps
        recovery at 20 ranges to bound cost. Called only by plan(), exactly once per
        rejected submission, as a single best-effort recovery attempt before giving up and
        surfacing the validation error to the model.
        """
        submission = SubmittedTour.model_validate(raw)
        recovered: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for step in submission.steps:

# Prompting fundamentals expressed in Waypoint

## 1. Explicit role and objective

Each workflow receives a narrow role rather than one universal vague prompt:

- evidence-first repository analyst;
- adaptive onboarding planner;
- safe first-contribution planner;
- credible issue investigator;
- evidence-rubric assessor.

The user question, onboarding role, objective, experience, and time budget are included
as runtime context instead of being replaced by predetermined answer templates.

## 2. Tool-oriented decomposition

The prompt tells the model to investigate before answering and explains when specialized
tools are preferable: overview/feature tools for repository summaries, entry-point tools
for startup, architecture tools for layers, and symbol/test/impact tools for focused
questions. Tool schemas constrain names, argument types, limits, and required fields.

This is agentic tool prompting rather than “put the entire repository in one prompt.”

## 3. Evidence grounding and epistemic discipline

The prompts distinguish:

- documentation evidence for product claims;
- implementation source for behavioral claims;
- verified syntax from static inference;
- possible calls from proven runtime behavior;
- proposed issues from maintainer-confirmed issues.

The model is instructed not to invent files, symbols, behavior, line numbers, or issues.
The backend then enforces inspected-range citations independently, so grounding is more
than a verbal instruction.

## 4. Prompt-injection boundary

Repository content is explicitly declared untrusted data. Prompts say never to follow

## Ask citation limits

Waypoint does not restrict an answer to one citation per file. A final answer may cite
multiple distinct passages from the same file. The frontend groups those passages under
one file card and initially opens the first passage.

| Citation or answer field | Limit |
|---|---:|
| Total citations in one answer | 30 |
| Citation title | 200 characters |
| Citation relevance explanation | 500 characters |
| Full answer | 30,000 characters |
| Answer basis | 2,000 characters |
| Suggested follow-up questions | 5 |
| Displayed citation excerpt | First 8 lines and at most 1,600 characters |

There is no explicit schema-level maximum number of lines in a citation. Each citation
must have a positive start line, an end line at or after the start line, and its entire
range must be contained in evidence previously inspected by the agent.

The direct `read_source` tool returns at most 250 lines per call, which practically
bounds citations based on that tool to its inspected range. Specialized semantic and
graph tools commonly return smaller evidence spans.

| Precision@k | acceptable retrieved files / retrieved files in first k | low noise |
| Path recall@k | acceptable paths found / all labeled acceptable paths | broad supporting coverage; deliberately demanding |
| Required-group recall@k | evidence groups satisfied / required groups | every independent reasoning hop is available |
| MRR | mean of `1 / rank of first relevant file` | useful evidence ranks early |
| AP@10 / MAP@10 | precision accumulated at relevant ranks, averaged per query/across queries | multiple relevant files rank early |
| nDCG@10 | discounted ranking gain normalized by the ideal order | better ordering receives more credit |
| Forbidden-hit rate | fraction of cases with a known distractor in top 10 | lower is better |
| Strict case pass | rank, group-recall, precision, and forbidden checks all pass | the complete case contract is satisfied |

The v2 retrieval score is the equal-weight mean of strict-case pass rate, required-group recall@10, MAP@10, MRR, nDCG@10, and `1 - forbidden-hit-rate`. This score replaces the old mean of Hit@5, Hit@10, MRR, and nDCG in newly generated operational scorecards.

2. Ask how an incoming request reaches a view function.

## 1. Explicit role and objective

Each workflow receives a narrow role rather than one universal vague prompt:

- evidence-first repository analyst;
- adaptive onboarding planner;
- safe first-contribution planner;
- credible issue investigator;
- evidence-rubric assessor.

The user question, onboarding role, objective, experience, and time budget are included
as runtime context instead of being replaced by predetermined answer templates.

## 2. Tool-oriented decomposition

The prompt tells the model to investigate before answering and explains when specialized
tools are preferable: overview/feature tools for repository summaries, entry-point tools
for startup, architecture tools for layers, and symbol/test/impact tools for focused
questions. Tool schemas constrain names, argument types, limits, and required fields.

This is agentic tool prompting rather than “put the entire repository in one prompt.”

## 3. Evidence grounding and epistemic discipline

The prompts distinguish:

- documentation evidence for product claims;
- implementation source for behavioral claims;
- verified syntax from static inference;
- possible calls from proven runtime behavior;
- proposed issues from maintainer-confirmed issues.

The model is instructed not to invent files, symbols, behavior, line numbers, or issues.
The backend then enforces inspected-range citations independently, so grounding is more
than a verbal instruction.

## Ask citation limits

Waypoint does not restrict an answer to one citation per file. A final answer may cite
multiple distinct passages from the same file. The frontend groups those passages under
one file card and initially opens the first passage.

| Citation or answer field | Limit |
|---|---:|
| Total citations in one answer | 30 |
| Citation title | 200 characters |
| Citation relevance explanation | 500 characters |
| Full answer | 30,000 characters |
| Answer basis | 2,000 characters |
| Suggested follow-up questions | 5 |
| Displayed citation excerpt | First 8 lines and at most 1,600 characters |

There is no explicit schema-level maximum number of lines in a citation. Each citation
must have a positive start line, an end line at or after the start line, and its entire
range must be contained in evidence previously inspected by the agent.

The direct `read_source` tool returns at most 250 lines per call, which practically
bounds citations based on that tool to its inspected range. Specialized semantic and
graph tools commonly return smaller evidence spans.

| Path recall@k | acceptable paths found / all labeled acceptable paths | broad supporting coverage; deliberately demanding |

| MRR | mean of `1 / rank of first relevant file` | useful evidence ranks early |

| nDCG@10 | discounted ranking gain normalized by the ideal order | better ordering receives more credit |
| Forbidden-hit rate | fraction of cases with a known distractor in top 10 | lower is better |

The v2 retrieval score is the equal-weight mean of strict-case pass rate, required-group recall@10, MAP@10, MRR, nDCG@10, and `1 - forbidden-hit-rate`. This score replaces the old mean of Hit@5, Hit@10, MRR, and nDCG in newly generated operational scorecards.
